newsitem.title: MEXICO: Economists see Mexican peso firmer by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Economists see Mexican peso firmer by year-end.

text.p: Economists say the Mexican peso will end the year stronger than previously predicted, and they have revised their forecasts down 17 centavos from last month, a central bank survey showed.
Banco de Mexico's monthly survey of 28 economists, obtained by Reuters, showed an average downward revision to 8.39 pesos to the dollar, from 8.56 forecast in last month's poll.
Expectations ranged from 8.10 to 8.65 pesos to the dollar.
The central bank asked 28 Mexico-based economists for their predictions on indicators including inflation, economic growth, the trade balance and foreign direct investment.
The economists' average forecast for year-end inflation was 16.67 percent, against last month's prediction of 16.93 percent. The highest forecast was 17.50 percent, and the lowest was 15.60 percent.
The economists raised their average 1997 GDP growth forecast to 5.00 pct from 4.91 percent. Forecasts ranged from 4.0 to 5.90 percent.
Their average prediction for third quarter GDP growth was 4.89 percent. The range of forecasts was 3.21-6.30 percent.
The economists see the 1997 trade surplus at $1.92 billion, down from the $2.37 billion they predicted in last month's survey.
They see Mexico's current account deficit at $6.29 billion, a little larger than the $6.03 billion forecast in last month's survey.
The economists' average forecast for foreign direct investment was $7.650 billion, down from $8.05 billion forecast in the previous poll.
